title: Colours as numbers
description:
Write:

```python
def to_hex_colour(r, g, b)     # (255, 136, 0) -> "#FF8800": each part as two upper-case hex digits
def from_hex_colour(text)      # "#ff8800" -> (255, 136, 0)
def grey(r, g, b)              # the brightness people see: 0.299 r + 0.587 g + 0.114 b, rounded
def image_bytes(width, height, bytes_per_pixel)   # the size of the uncompressed image
```

You may use `int(text, 16)` and the `:02X` format here (`f"{136:02X}"` is `"88"`): you already wrote those yourself in 2.04. `text[1:3]` is the two characters after the `#`.
hints: `f"{r:02X}"` writes a number as two upper-case hex digits; put three of them after a `#`.
Going back, `int(text[1:3], 16)` reads the red part, `text[3:5]` green and `text[5:7]` blue. The image size is width × height × bytes per pixel.
